brief.analysis: The strongest case for a changed world: Europe and allies committed to lift defense spending toward 3.5% of GDP by 2035 with global military outlays at record highs, a multi-year rearmament that structurally lifts where defense stocks trade versus the market. The tell is direct: measured against its own rising trend the ratio is barely stretched (well under the flat-average reading, and the two disagree by more than the usual margin), which is hard evidence the average itself is climbing. The 19% fall the 5-year average implies is a statistical trap, not a target.
brief.report_line: Avoid shorting defense-versus-S&P: a decade-long rearmament cycle is lifting the baseline, and the ratio is only stretched against a flat average that is itself drifting up.

brief.analysis: The strongest case for a changed world: metals and mining is being called the front of a new supercycle, up roughly 90% in a year and beating chips and big tech, as AI data centers, electrification and copper scarcity drive metals to fresh highs. The dislocation has already unwound — the near-term target is met, and against its own steeply rising trend the ratio is essentially not stretched at all, meaning the average has moved up under it. Shorting back to the old 5-year average (a 17% fall) is fighting a live secular bull market.
brief.report_line: Avoid shorting miners-versus-S&P: the metals supercycle has re-rated the whole sector, the stretch is already gone, and the old 5-year average is no longer a valid target.

brief.analysis: The strongest case for a changed world: silver has already run far ahead in a genuine catch-up, driven by real industrial demand (solar, EVs, electronics) against tight supply, not just speculation, so its higher standing versus gold may be partly permanent. The extreme stretch has already largely deflated — the near-term target is met, the trend-adjusted reading is near neutral, and the two readings agree there is no hidden further drift. What is left is a modest pull toward the longer average that is worth a small position, not the full 17% the old average implies.
brief.report_line: Short silver-versus-gold in small size for the remaining pullback only; the big move is already spent and silver's industrial demand story argues against a full return to the 5-year average.

brief.analysis: The strongest case for a changed world: the AI build-out is the largest private capital deployment on record and is still growing into 2026-27, with chips capturing the biggest single slice of that spend, so chips leading the Nasdaq may be the new normal rather than a stretch. The near-term snap toward the 200-day average (+14%) is plausible and the base rate is decent, but the full 5-year average (a 67% fall in chips versus the Nasdaq) assumes an AI leadership that has structurally re-rated simply hands it all back. Trade the shallow target, treat the deep one as a mirage.
brief.report_line: Short chips-versus-Nasdaq for a modest bounce back to the 200-day average only, sized down, because the record AI spending cycle means the deep 5-year target is likely no longer reachable.
